units.translation: in anapaests, which also bear the contracted form ἀκόντων [unwilling], as Pr. 277 οὐκ ἀκούσαις ἐπεθώνξας [you did not heed my warning]. Similarly, Sophocles in Tr. 1263 in anapaests preferred to say τελέουσ᾽ ἀεκούσιον ἔργον [accomplishing an unwilling deed] rather than ἀκούσιον [unwilling].
to set foot upon this land of unwilling men,
you did not heed my warning

where M has διπλόμεσθα ἐπτάναξ [we are destroyed, O lord], which Robortellus corrected. On the two other places where deλntog has been introduced by scribal error, see under the word ἄεπτος [not to be approached].
to the house, unexpected, as justice may lead.
we are destroyed; unexpected things, O lord, we suffer,
the ever-flowing rivers of the earth.
from there the life-giving blood, increasing, flourishes for mortals.
to the leaf-nourishing banks of Simois.
